surprises.description: The problem development loan grew beyond the preview’s $32.8 million NPL reference: nonperforming loans reached $39.2 million, or 80 basis points of loans, with about $30 million tied to one waterfront condo project. The increase is concerning, though management said the roughly $21 million net exposure is fully reserved.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Nonperforming loans rose to $39.2 million or 80 basis points of total loans (up from 74 bps),” with “$30 million” being commercial and roughly two-thirds tied to a single problem waterfront condo development project; management said the “~$21 million net exposure” is “fully reserved.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview identified “the $32.8M NPL bucket” and said resolution, partial charge-off, or further migration was “the biggest single-name risk in the print.”

surprises.description: Provision was higher than the preview’s expected range: it came in at about 0.4% of loans annualized, versus a forecast of 0.2%–0.25%, because of a specific reserve on one commercial relationship.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q3 provision for credit losses was $4.8 million (~0.4% of loans annualized), above the 0.2%-0.25% forecast, driven by a specific reserve on one commercial relationship.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview’s estimate build used “Provision (organic) $3.0M” and its base case expected “credit stable.”

surprises.description: The anticipated acquired-loan day-2 CECL charge does not appear in the reported EPS bridge: GAAP EPS was $0.80 and adjusted EPS was $0.92 after excluding $2.7 million of after-tax merger costs. The preview had identified a possible $3.5–$4.4 million CECL provision as a significant additional Q3 charge.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted EPS excluding $2.7 million after-tax merger costs was $0.92,” compared with “$0.80 per diluted share” GAAP EPS.
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said it was uncertain “whether the day-2 CECL provision lands in Q3,” and estimated a likely provision on acquired non-PCD loans of “~$3.5–4.4M.”

surprises.description: Organic loan growth was much stronger than the preview’s seasonally soft-quarter framing: growth excluding High Point was 10.5% annualized, with commercial loans growing nearly 21% annualized, and management said this exceeded its full-year forecast range.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Organic net loan growth was $116.6 million (10.5% annualized) excluding High Point, above the full-year forecast range of 4.5%-5.5%, with commercial loans growing nearly 21% annualized.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said management had “flagged Q3 as seasonally soft” and that the full-year outlook required “a strong Q4.”

surprises.description: Margin exceeded the preview’s estimate, and the increase was not solely reflected in the reported margin including purchase accounting: NIM reached 3.82% versus the preview’s 3.75% estimate, while NIM excluding accretion rose 5 basis points to 3.76%.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Net interest margin rose 11 basis points to 3.82% (3.76% excluding purchase accounting accretion, up 5 bps).”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview estimated “NIM 3.75%” and flagged that a 3.80%+ result “mostly [from] accretion” would be lower quality than core expansion.
